The global copper market is extremely tight:
China's copper import premium over London Metal Exchange (LME) prices has surpassed $200 per ton, the largest premium on record.
The Yangshan premium, named after a Shanghai port that serves as a major hub for Chinese copper imports, has more than doubled over the last 3 months.
Since the beginning of 2026, this figure has surged +700%.
Furthermore, the premium of spot prices over three-month futures on the LME widened to $217 per ton, the largest since mid-August.
This has been driven by strong Chinese copper demand and domestic inventories falling below typical seasonal levels.
At the same time, expectations of potential US tariffs on refined copper have redirected hundreds of thousands of tons of copper to the US, leaving global inventories heavily concentrated in the country.
The physical copper supply squeeze is far from over.

$SPY’s monthly BX trender just closed red.
70% of the time that means a dip. 30% of the time it means a crash.
Here’s how I see things playing out
We’ve officially broken the $758 swing low on the daily time frame, which is not ideal. We’ve been covering this zone for the past couple of weeks, and it was a very important level short term.
There’s a chance price bounces from here and sweeps back up to all-time highs much sooner than I’m expecting. Historically, though, that only happens about 20% to 25% of the time, so I’m not banking on it.
Now that support has broken, if price can’t get back above $760 within the next week, it will most likely keep redistributing down toward $740, the lower smart money zone on the daily.
My biggest concern right now is that the monthly BX trender closed red.
When we switch over to the monthly chart, you’ll notice that over the past decade, a red monthly BX trender doesn’t necessarily mean a total market crash. (image 2)
Normally, it means a continued correction of about 5% from where we are.
The most extensive pullback was January 2022 to October 2022, when the market went into a full bear market for multiple months before finding a potential bottom. Before that, there was 2020, where the market dropped about 26% because of COVID, and a correction in 2018, where it dropped about 12%.
So looking at the past decade, a red monthly BX trender doesn’t necessarily mean the market is going to crash. It does tend to mean that the broader buying pressure is getting sucked out.
The last two times this happened were March 2026 and April 2025. Both times, we saw a continued sell-off for about a month, followed by a V-shaped recovery.
This doesn’t mean we need to go into panic mode. But like I said at the start of this analysis, a continued pullback of 2% to 3% is very much on the table.
Looking back at the decade before that, from 2000 to 2011, there were multiple monthly BX flips. (image 3)
Most of the time, like in 2005 and 2006, price just kept working its way up. But three major pullbacks happened during that decade. The first was the dot-com bubble, when the market dropped about 44% after the monthly BX turned red. Then came the 2008 financial crisis, when the market dropped about 53% after the monthly BX turned red.
I don’t want you to be worried. A red monthly BX doesn’t mean the market is going to crash. That only happens about 30% of the time when the monthly BX turns red.
What we do need to understand is that if the market is going to crash, it will happen during a red monthly BX trender. So when the BX trender is red, we need to be more careful than we are in a bull cycle.
That doesn’t mean we trade any differently. We still focus on smart money zones, and we still focus on quality setups. But there’s no reason to over-leverage positions or load up on call options. When this happens, a higher level of caution comes into my plan.
So with all that said, where does this leave us?
The most important thing to remember is that structure matters more than the cycle or the monthly BX. In every case we talked about where the market bounced after the monthly BX turned red, structure held. In every case where the market went into a serious downturn, structure gave out. So as long as structure holds, I see a low chance of a major 10% to 15% correction in the S&P 500.
On the daily chart right now, there’s a good chance we get another 2% pullback down to about $740. That would be a strong short-term area, and it’s normally where we’d see price bounce. If you use the 33 fair value band on the weekly time frame, that’s a major support too.
If $728 breaks, that’s where we get into serious correction territory. From there, I’d look for a sell-off into the weekly institutional buy zone at $684 to $660, with the smart money zone between $660 and $650. That would fill the downside gap from April 2026.
Like I said, I wouldn’t worry about that yet, because we’re still showing structure on all the smaller time frames. If the smaller time frames start to give out, that’s when we need to be aware that a broader correction could happen.

AI is burning Big Tech's free cash flow:
The combined CapEx of Amazon, $AMZN, Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $META, and Microsoft, $MSFT, rose +$36.9 billion in Q3 2026, to a record $201.9 billion.
This figure has more than doubled over the last 12 months and is up +356% since Q1 2024.
Big Tech has now spent $1.6 trillion on CapEx over the last 3 years.
Meanwhile, the combined free cash flow of these companies fell -$33.1 billion last quarter, to -$26.4 billion, its lowest on record.
Free cash flow among these firms has dropped -$88.2 billion over the last year.
Only Microsoft reported positive free cash flow in Q3.
Looking ahead, these 4 companies plan to spend another $232 billion on CapEx in Q4, potentially lifting their combined CapEx to a record $740 billion in 2026.
Big Tech is undertaking one of the largest infrastructure buildouts in history.

The FBI named the unit behind the $6.3B Binance hack. TraderTraitor, not Lazarus.
North Korea has stolen roughly $6.75B in crypto since 2017. They nearly matched nine years of work in a few hours on Thursday.
And they're doing it with fewer attacks every year, not more. In 2025 they took 76% of all exchange theft value worldwide while running 74% fewer operations than the year before.
Same unit hit Bitget for $351.6M in September and Bybit for $1.5B last year. The two largest crypto hacks in history both belong to them.
The timing nobody flagged: the US Treasury sanctioned North Korea's fake remote IT worker network on October 28. Binance got drained on October 29.
The UN estimates those fake workers alone bring the regime $250M to $600M a year, separate from anything they steal.

第二，我依然认为赵长鹏此前的公开回应是冲动的。
我一直有个观点，一个人的公开表达，是要看别人怎么理解，而不是看你怎么表达，有比例的共识的理解就是你作为发言人必须接受和承担的代价。
因为当一句话被说出口，它就不再完全属于说话的人了。
你可以解释自己的本意，但不能要求所有人都按照你的本意去理解。
cz可能承受着巨大的压力，也理解人在压力之下难免冲动。
但理解不代表不能评价。
选择必有代价，冲动当然也是一种选择。
第三，我确实认为何一是个非常厉害的女人。
尤其是她那句，大意是向各位股东汇报，目前还没到需要卖出SpaceX股份来填补窟窿的时候。
我觉得这个回复非常漂亮。
没有刻意回避问题，也没有过多解释，而是用一句话回应了外界对资金状况的担忧。
当然，我不懂币圈，也不知道这件事究竟存在多大的实际风险，所以不打算装作自己什么都懂。
至于今天何一亲自回复我，确实有点出乎意料。
我一个喜欢读几本书，又特别好为人师的小博主，本来只是借着新闻谈谈国家利益与道德的问题。开头提到FBI的结论，也只是想说，权威值得尊重，但权威不等于绝对真理，并不是在否认朝鲜作案。
早知道会惊动这些大人物，我可能就不发了。毕竟我这个人虽然喜欢装逼，但也知道自己几斤几两。
不过话说回来，身份有高低，观点却不应该因此分贵贱。
我可以尊重一个人，也可以欣赏一个人，但不代表我必须同意他的每一句话。
同样，我也希望别人可以不同意我。
最后，基于今天何一的回复，我是真心希望币安能够平安度过这次风波。
毕竟我始终觉得，一个人最难得的能力，不是永远做出正确的选择，而是在选择之后，能够承担它带来的一切。
这句话送给我自己。
这次事件给我最大的思考是赚钱的意义是什么？如果是改变世界，我可以理解，这会是下篇日记的内容。（日记2026.11.01石）
